newsitem.title: USA: Positron ends deal with GE unit.
newsitem.headline: Positron ends deal with GE unit.

text.p: Positron Corp said Friday it will not pursue its acquisition of some medical scanner assets of a General Electric Corp unit and will instead focus on securing financing to alleviate its liquidity problems.
Positron and GE had announced a deal under which Positron would buy GE Medical's positron emission tomography (PET) assets for $25 million and 10 percent of Positron's outstanding common stock.
earlier this month, Positron said its auditors had substantial doubts that it could continue as a going concern, and Positron President and Chief Executive Werner Haas resigned.
Positron said today it will focus on providing working capital to manufacture and ship its nine previously announced orders, and will set its sights on the emerging cardiac PET market.

Chairman Gary Wood said in a statement, "With managed care taking on a more dominant role in U.S. medicine, we believe a great opportunity exists for PET technology since it produces better care at a lower cost."
